close_reason: Decision record landed at panic_message_not_in_response doc — explicit cross-reference to bd:JMAP-jfia.14 plus rationale defending the recursive-walk shape against future single-field-check 'simplification'.
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/lib.rs:683-705 — the panic_message_not_in_response test recursively walks the entire methodResponse args Value (object values, array elements, strings) and asserts that no String anywhere in the tree contains the canary literal "deliberate test panic".

A future contributor will reasonably suggest "simplify — just check args.description, that's where panic-payloads land in the current implementation". That suggestion is WRONG and the recursive walk should be defended.

Why recursive walk is the correct shape (the inline comment makes the argument; this is a decision record):

  - The current implementation produces serverFail with description = "internal error" (a static string, no panic-payload leak). A targeted description check would pass today.
  - A future refactor could surface panic-payload text through a typed `context` field, an `innerError` nested object, an `extras` map, or any other field that slipped past a single-field check.
  - A canary-leak test that only checks the field where the leak currently doesn't land gives no protection against drift. It encodes the current implementation rather than the security invariant.
  - The recursive walk encodes the actual invariant: "panic-payload text does not leak to the wire, ANYWHERE in the response shape". That holds across refactors of the error shape.

Test shape to preserve. Worth a decision record so a future "simplify" pass does not narrow the assertion to a single field check.

Same pattern recommended for the BackendChangesError leak test that JMAP-jfia.1 calls for: walk the entire wire response for the canary, do not target a single field.
title: panic_message_not_in_response recursive walk is the correct security test shape
